A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOLID research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and isolated reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: V2 reports original distillation, customization, layer-selection, sensitivity, and correlation experiments in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports black-box adversarial-attack evaluations in Appendix B.10.

M1.justification: SOLID already appears in v2 Section 4.2. V3 Section 3.2 retains its bottom-layer search, initialization-based distillation-difficulty score, and stopping threshold. The revised framing does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 Appendix B.10 adds membership inference on AG News, attribute inference on PersonalReddit, and adversarial prompt testing. This is a supplementary extension beyond distillation and customization; the existing functionality benchmarks and customization tasks remain.

E2.justification: V3 Table 3 adds DarkneTZ to the attack-dataset scaling comparison, which v2 Appendix C.6 reported for SOLID alone. Table 14 also introduces a Gold Std. comparison, with LED identified for prompt attacks. The principal DarkneTZ, SAP-DP, and fully-secured comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B.10 introduces SPV-MIA/AUC, attribute-inference top-3 accuracy, and AutoDAN/keyword-based attack-success protocols. V3 also revises the set-size disclosure: Table 7 lists 4,066 evaluation items versus 1,516 in v2 Table 5, although its composition and purpose conflict with the accompanying validation/evaluation descriptions. These disclosures do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds tests asking whether protection extends to membership inference, attribute inference, and prompt attacks, and extends the scaling analysis with DarkneTZ. The layer-placement, secured-size, tolerance, DD-correlation, and OPT-350M analyses already existed in v2, including its appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions specify DD seeds 20, 42, and 1234, one distillation seed for Llama2-70B, and three for the other models. Correlation reporting is retained; v3 introduces no new stated uncertainty-estimation, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 and matched detailed appendix results are unchanged. V3 Table 3 newly reports DarkneTZ scaling ADRs, including 89.1 at 100k and 96.9 at 500k. Table 14 adds adversarial-attack scores, but labels the row discussed as SOLID as SCARA, leaving that row's attribution unclear.

T1.justification: The transition theorem, substantive assumptions, DD derivation, and Appendix A proof are retained. Remarks move from the main text to Appendix A.5, while equations are condensed and renumbered without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The central claim of strong distillation resistance with preserved customization remains. V3 replaces the introduction's single-layer formulation with a few or minimal bottom layers, foregrounds DD-guided trade-off optimization, and removes discussion of alternative positions from the contribution list. Broad deployment advocacy becomes more explicitly focused on technical findings.

C2.justification: V3 newly states that SOLID offers limited protection against other black-box attacks and attributes SAP-DP's advantage to output perturbation. It also identifies layer-level selection as a limitation. The OPT-350M limitation is retained and promoted; v2's substantive discussion of regulatory, hybrid, and open-weight alternatives is removed.

D1.justification: V3 adds a SOLID repository link, source-composition details for the already reported larger attack datasets, expanded validation descriptions, and implementation references for the new adversarial tests. Existing optimizer, training, hardware, and software settings remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning against logit-based extraction through Carlini et al. and Finlayson et al., plus literature supporting the new adversarial tests. It removes citations and discussion associated with broader privacy alternatives, including DeepSeek-R1. The central relationship to layer-partition protection methods remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten from position-paper advocacy into a technical narrative. Related work moves after experiments, existing DD analysis becomes a main-text research question, theoretical remarks move to the appendix, and Alternative Views and the Impact Statement give way to Limitations and Acknowledgements.

P2.justification: Appendix prose and proofs change from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive changes to table-caption placement and figure positioning. V3 adds Figures 6 and 11 to visualize existing results, promotes the DD/OPT figure into the main text, and adds scaling, dataset-composition, and adversarial-result tables.

improvement.justification: V3 makes existing DD validation and the OPT-350M limitation easier to find, adds useful evidence bounding protection against other attacks, and supplies missing dataset-composition and code-access information. These provide a limited net improvement. The SCARA/SOLID mismatch in Table 14 and conflicting validation-set descriptions weaken precision and temper the gains.
